correctness.rationale: For each interior triple, every record indicator outside its three positions is independent of that triple's relative order. Conditional on a record at the first, middle or last position, the six pattern probabilities follow respectively from a beta-uniform integral, a beta-i conditional splitting, or equiprobability of the other two ranks. The local covariance vector has numerators (3i+1,7-3i,3i-5,3i-5,1-3i,1-3i) over 6i(i-1)(i+1); summing i=2..n-1 gives the exact six formulas. Independent exact rational direct permutation enumeration confirms 36 finite-n covariances and 108 local joint probabilities, and symbolic telescoping confirms all six; these computations corroborate rather than replace the infinite analytic argument. Claims are confined to iid atomless data, n>=3.

originality.rationale: The complete six-coordinate covariance with the number of upper records is not entailed by the inspected joint distribution of the four unoriented local classifications or by record marginal laws. Full ten-page Chen–Cheng source inspected. An identified earlier result gives the same covariance only for the sum of the two peak orientations (also matched by a record/BST statistic), and this coarsening is excluded from the originality claim. The six-way orientation split and the n=5 sign boundary for 132 remain distinct, with plausible but unexcluded historical implicit derivations.
residual_risks: An older multivariate record/permutation generating function might implicitly produce all six mixed covariances without listing these coefficients.

value.rationale: The six length-three ordinal patterns form the smallest full family distinguishing local order orientations, a natural ingredient of nonparametric serial randomness tests. Total upper records measure global sequential extremes. Their complete direction-resolved cross-covariance reveals that the two peak orientations behave differently, with the 132 term crossing precisely at n=5 even though the aggregated peak covariance is always positive. This is a motivated natural classification with a finite-sample sign boundary and distribution-free limiting reference vector, not a renamed marginal or a recomputation of a known coarse statistic.
